paragraphs.text: The newest Buffer operating update adds [[SaaSOperatingTransparency]] to the startup and SaaS cluster. [[JoelGascoigne]] reports [[Buffer]]'s August 2015 state through a multi-metric dashboard: 2.67 million registered users, 211,520 monthly active users, $624,196 MRR, $7.49M ARR, $2.79 million cash, 42 team members across 33 cities, 14 open roles, about 1,500 applications, product launches, support volume, customer happiness, and response times. The source strengthens [[SmallProductTeamBalance]] by showing Buffer splitting product and engineering into autonomous 4-6 person teams while still needing single-area focus for people stretched across several teams. It also connects customer-led product learning to shipping velocity: a customer note about Buffer for Video and link-thumbnail updates is used as evidence that recent features made users feel heard.

The newest Buffer source adds [[RemoteWork]] as a practical workplace-culture system rather than only a location preference. [[CourtneySeiter]] presents [[Buffer]] as a remote-company case where productivity depends on trust over visibility, inclusion for non-office workers, explicit communication, video connection, time-zone and WiFi tooling, and periodic physical presence. The source also strengthens [[AttentionManagement]], [[WorkHabits]], and [[WorkplaceCollaboration]] by showing that remote workers need start/end rituals, meeting batching, intentional serendipity, positive intent in text-heavy communication, and deliberate resistance to Slack-driven false urgency. The inspected images were mostly decorative home-office, quote-card, separator, and author assets; the quote cards repeat prose claims about closing the laptop, remote-work guilt, communication without body language, and time-zone difficulty.

The newest Firefox source adds browser-market concentration to the wiki's open-web and platform-power material. The Official Unofficial Firefox Blog frames [[Chrome]] as a good but over-dominant browser route into [[Google]]'s search and display-ad business, citing roughly four times [[Firefox]]'s desktop market share in the 2016-2017 StatCounter window. [[Firefox]] and [[Mozilla]] are presented as the counterweight: improved performance, lower memory use, private browsing with tracking protection, Firefox Focus, nonprofit governance, and a healthy-web mission. This strengthens [[WebCentralization]] by showing that platform concentration can operate inside the browser layer itself, not only through app, assistant, cloud, commerce, or feed-based [[BrowserBypass]]. The duplicate Stay Puft images are decorative campaign framing; the GIF shows Chrome-colored machine imagery; the small chart supports the source's Firefox-versus-Chrome memory-use claim.

The newest 8VC source adds an executive-timing layer to the startup-scaling cluster. [[JoeLonsdale]] argues that very early technology startups should rely on intense builders, tight culture fit, rapid product iteration, and advisor scaffolding rather than full-time veteran operators. [[StartupHiringAtScale]], [[ExecutiveHiring]], [[ProductMarketFit]], [[StartupScaling]], and [[CEOScalingRole]] now distinguish premature executive process from the later moment when revenue, product-market clarity, and repeatable functions make experienced sales, HR, engineering-management, marketing, finance, strategy, and related leaders valuable. [[8VC]] becomes the venture-firm and publication context for the advice. The three inspected local images are decorative alternate crops of the same bird illustration.

The newest Lightspeed source adds a beautifully broken product layer to the startup and consumer-product cluster. [[AdamTaussig]] argues that early products can be obviously flawed yet valuable when users keep returning because the core problem is acute. [[BeautifullyBrokenProducts]] names that pattern: [[Uber]] overcame bad rides, delays, surge pricing, and pickup friction because San Francisco transport alternatives were weak; [[StitchFix]] users could retry after poor boxes because affordable personal shopping was compelling; [[Twitter]]'s fail whale made infrastructure failure legible while demand kept growing; [[HQTrivia]] turned live-video lag into a meme rather than an immediate adoption killer; and early [[Android]] users tolerated clunkiness because openness, cost, and rapid improvement mattered. The inspected images mostly support the examples: a decorative broken-glass lead photo, early Uber positioning, small Stitch Fix and Android visuals, a small HQ host image, and a Medium clap animation.

The newest Boz source adds a time-stewardship layer to the wiki's attention, productivity, and collaboration material. [[AndrewBosworth]] argues that time is more scarce than money, so interruptions, messages, quick visits, and meetings should clear a high burden before they claim another person's attention. [[AttentionManagement]] now includes social context-switch costs and urgent-over-important drift, while [[WorkplaceCollaboration]] and [[ProductReviewMeetings]] gain meeting-owner responsibilities: clear purpose, appropriate size, agenda, expected outcomes, notes, accountability, feedback, attendance curation, and short recurring-meeting expirations. The source contains no image references.

The earlier Boz product-review source adds a product-review-meeting layer to the wiki's work and product-leadership material. [[ProductReviewMeetings]] captures the P Rules as a power-aware facilitation model: avoid piling on, pedantry, pontificating, prescription, permission capture, pessimism, and interruptions so review helps the team reason without taking away ownership or presenter agency. [[AndrewBosworth]] is represented as the authorial entity behind the rules. [[ProductLeadership]], [[WorkplaceCollaboration]], and [[PerformativeMeetingBehavior]] distinguish useful senior critique from senior-looking behavior that makes presenters defensive, shifts responsibility upward, or suppresses candor. The source contains no image references.

The newest CB Insights source adds a broad failure-corpus view to the wiki's startup material. New [[StartupFailurePatterns]] groups hundreds of shutdown narratives into recurring mechanisms: weak [[ProductMarketFit]], exhausted [[StartupRunway]], premature scaling, market-timing mismatch, platform dependence, hardware and operational complexity, regulatory or legal shocks, governance failures, and business-model fragility. [[CBInsights]] becomes the research-publisher entity behind the corpus. The source strengthens earlier single-company lessons from Maderight, Hardbound, Juicero, Bump, and Microsoft by showing that startup failure is usually compound rather than one clean mistake, while also qualifying post-mortems as retrospective evidence shaped by founder self-explanation, investor framing, journalism, and company shutdown notices. The remote hero image returned HTTP 403 and could not be inspected.

The newest Wulc source adds an advertising data-trading layer to the wiki's adtech material. New [[DataManagementPlatform]] captures first-party DMPs that process advertiser-owned data into requested labels without default resale, and third-party DMPs that aggregate data-provider inputs, apply their own label logic, sell label data toward DSP demand, and share revenue back. [[DataMonetization]] and [[ProgrammaticAdvertising]] now include ADX-mediated DMP-to-DSP label flows, the pricing concern that impression-based data charging can lift traffic prices while understating data value, and the privacy constraints around PII, opt-out, retention, sparse-data reidentification, and differential privacy. [[BehavioralData]] and [[BehavioralTargeting]] are sharpened by a value-density hierarchy: conversion and cart behavior outrank search and clicks, which outrank page views, sharing, and forced ad exposure. The four embedded diagrams were inspected and used as evidence for first/second/third-party data relations, first-party and third-party DMP business models, and ADX-mediated data trading.

The newest Wulc source adds the portfolio-construction section of Zhang Xiaoyu's personal investing course to the wiki's finance material. [[AssetAllocation]] now includes asset-class roles, maximum-drawdown control, model portfolio tradeoffs, and rebalancing rather than only behavioral diversification; [[PersonalInvestorStrategy]] becomes a target-portfolio discipline built from simple templates, low-cost passive products, annual or threshold-based rebalancing, and skepticism toward vague investing language. New [[FactorInvesting]] captures size, value, low-volatility, dividend, quality, and momentum exposure as a semi-passive middle path that still needs diversification because factor performance rotates. [[IndexFundStrategy]] is sharpened by broad-based, industry, and strategy-index distinctions plus an inspected screenshot comparing off-exchange and exchange-traded fund channels by mechanism, pricing, purchase route, fees, eligible fund range, and minimum investment.

The newest Wulc source adds the investment-tools and self-limitation sections of Zhang Xiaoyu's personal investing course to the wiki's finance material. [[PersonalInvestorStrategy]] now includes five ordinary-investor principles: diversify, use passive-first implementation, lower costs, remain patient, and avoid what one does not understand. [[IndexFundStrategy]] is sharpened by a market-context caveat: U.S.-market index-fund advice should not be copied mechanically into A-share markets, and even broad indexes can suffer long recovery periods after overvalued entry points. [[InvestmentRiskDiscipline]] gains margin-of-safety discipline, fee-drag compounding, negative-compounding risk, and outside-income resilience, while [[BehavioralRiskJudgment]] adds luck-versus-skill review, written thesis records, advice-incentive filtering, and independent decision space. No image references were present in the source Markdown.

The newest Wulc source adds Unix-like process-lifecycle cleanup to the wiki's systems material. New [[OrphanProcess]] distinguishes still-running child processes whose parent has exited from [[ZombieProcess]], terminated children whose parent has not called `wait` or `waitpid` to collect status. The practical synthesis is parent-focused: orphans are normally safe because `init` adopts and reaps them, while zombies can retain PID, exit-status, and CPU-time metadata until enough leaked process IDs prevent new process creation. The source includes a `ps -A -o stat,ppid,pid,cmd | grep -e '^[Zz]'` detection command and recommends terminating the zombie's parent so `init` can take over cleanup. No image references were present in the source Markdown.

The newest Wulc source adds a foundational concurrency taxonomy to the wiki's software-systems material. New [[ConcurrentProgramming]], [[ParallelProgramming]], and [[DistributedProgramming]] distinguish scheduler-mediated pseudo-parallelism, multi-core simultaneous execution, and networked execution across physically separated machines, with inspected diagrams grounding each model. New [[InterprocessCommunication]] and [[MessagePassing]] capture the source's shared-state versus copied-message tradeoff: shared writable state needs protection such as locks, while messages cost memory but improve consistency and fit distributed environments. [[ConcurrencyFailureModes]], [[Deadlock]], [[Starvation]], and [[RaceCondition]] now give the wiki a compact vocabulary for circular waits, unfair non-progress, and timing-dependent state corruption, and [[Python]] gains [[PythonConcurrencyLibraries]] as a 2016 introductory module map covering `threading`, `multiprocessing`, Parallel Python, and Celery.

The newest Wulc reading source adds [[SpeedReadingMethod]] to the wiki's learning-method material. The method treats nonfiction reading as three passes: evaluate whether the book deserves attention, speed-read for structure and concepts, and deep-read selected parts only when they are worth remembering or outputting. This sharpens [[FocusedReading]] by adding pre-reading evaluation, visual scanning, semantic-unit navigation, and concept hunting; it strengthens [[ActiveLearning]] by making notes, reactions, oral explanation, writing, and teaching the test of effective reading. It also complements [[LearningByWriting]] because drafting is presented as a way to clarify vague reading impressions and separate imperfect first creation from later evaluation. No image references were present in the source Markdown.

The newest Jeanette Head source adds a disagreement-selection layer to the wiki's collaboration and review material. [[WorkplaceCollaboration]] now includes a frame for deciding when to press, let go, or pursue a useful losing debate: developers should ask whether they can influence the outcome, whether the issue is worth the time and emotional cost, and what concrete product or team gain justifies raising the stakes. [[CodeReviewPractice]] gains a reviewer-side triage rule: distinguish codebase standards, material performance issues, and readability problems from personal style preferences, and prefer conversation over line-by-line critique when someone is ramping into project norms. [[JeanetteHead]] and [[AtomicObject]] anchor the source; the remote lead photograph was inspected and treated as decorative.

The newest Taresky source extends the wiki's crypto-yield material from centralized exchange lending and funding-rate arbitrage into DeFi stablecoin mining. New [[StablecoinYieldFarming]] frames stablecoin liquidity as a lower-volatility way to earn from traders' swaps, borrowing, platform incentives, and compounding rather than from directional coin bets, while [[LiquidityProvision]], [[AutomatedMarketMaker]], and [[ImpermanentLoss]] explain the DEX mechanics underneath: pools need depth, AMMs quote from balances, and liquidity providers accept rebalancing opportunity cost. New [[DeFiRiskStack]] is the strongest addition: the source treats "stable" yield as exposed to fiat on-ramp scrutiny, exchange custody, wallet and seed-phrase mistakes, stablecoin failure, chain centralization, smart-contract bugs, malicious token approvals, misleading APY, vault layering, OTC exit risk, tax ambiguity, and unknown unknowns. [[BeltFinance]] and [[BeefyFinance]] are captured only as time-sensitive process examples, and [[CryptoWalletSecurity]], [[Taresky]], and [[Binance]] now reflect seed-phrase, hardware-wallet, authorization, on-ramp, and BSC trust-model details from the source.

The newest Taresky source adds a crypto-yield and arbitrage layer to the wiki's investing material. New [[CryptoArbitrage]] frames exchange lending and funding-rate collection as yield supplied by borrowers and leveraged speculators rather than magic passive income, while preserving the article's important qualification that "risk-free" only refers to neutralized price exposure, not exchange failure, stablecoin failure, liquidation, spread, execution, or behavioral risk. New [[ExchangeLending]], [[PerpetualFutures]], [[FundingRateArbitrage]], and [[DeltaNeutralStrategy]] explain the mechanics: exchanges such as [[Bitfinex]], [[OKX]], and [[Binance]] intermediate lending markets, perpetual contracts use funding payments to tether derivative prices to spot, and a spot-plus-short-perpetual position can collect funding while reducing directional exposure. The inspected screenshots support the source's March 2024 bull-market context: USDT lending APY examples near 20-46%, Coinglass heatmaps with many assets above 50% annualized funding, extreme high/low funding rankings, and a captured explanation of why gambler demand, survivor bias, and time-lagged awareness can keep yields high temporarily.

The newest Guangzhengli source sharpens the wiki's AI coding vocabulary. New [[ContextCoding]] names the disciplined version of AI-assisted programming: the developer still uses AI heavily, but the central work is giving the model useful and current context through files, rules, RAG, grep/search, MCP tools, logs, documentation, tests, and context-budget awareness. [[VibeCoding]] is now more explicitly split between Karpathy's original no-review, result-steered, throwaway-project meaning and the broader popular use for coding-agent acceleration. [[GitHubCopilot]], [[Cursor]], and [[ClaudeCode]] form a tool-evolution line: open-file and cursor-local context, project RAG and rules, then command-line whole-project exploration through Unix tools. The seven embedded screenshots were inspected and used as evidence for the original Karpathy definition, Claude Code `/context` budgeting, Leo's non-technical production failure arc, and @levelsio's experienced-developer AI leverage case.

The newest beepb00p source adds a personal-data infrastructure layer to the wiki. New [[DataLiberation]], [[PersonalDataMirror]], and [[PersonalDataInfrastructure]] capture a practical stack where devices, phone apps, cloud services, APIs, scraping, GDPR exports, manual downloads, and direct filesystem/database access feed local files, then [[HumanProgrammingInterface]] turns those files into reusable modules for [[Promnesia]], [[Orger]], notebooks, APIs, spreadsheets, and metrics stores. [[Beepb00p]] is anchored as the practitioner-author of the map, while [[Android]] gains a data-ownership qualification: app sandboxing can be protective but can also force rooting when users need access to their own app-private data. The embedded SVG diagram was inspected and used as evidence for data-flow layers, WIP paths, dead-service continuity, anti-API friction, and downstream use cases.

The newest Antirez source adds a forceful pro-adoption counterweight to the wiki's AI-coding cautions. New [[Antirez]] anchors the source as a Redis creator and systems programmer who values hand-written minimal software but argues that recent LLM capability changes the practical shape of programming. [[AICodingPractice]] now includes his shift from line-by-line implementation toward problem representation, prompting, inspection, and guidance. [[ClaudeCode]] gains concrete Redis-adjacent examples: linenoise UTF-8 and terminal-cell testing, Redis test-flake debugging, a C embedding-inference library, and Redis Streams work reproduced from a design document. [[PracticalLLMUse]] is strengthened by his advice to test AI tools seriously over weeks, while [[AIDependencySkillAtrophy]] is narrowed: the risk is not AI use itself but replacing the practices that still build judgment, taste, and maintenance ownership. The source contained no Markdown image references.

The newest Zhao CS source adds packet-level MPLS L2VPN detail to the wiki's networking material. New [[L2VPNDummyVLAN]] captures the key behavior: in the successful IOS XR EoMPLS Type 4 case, a dummy VLAN is an 802.1Q VLAN ID 0 tag carrying 802.1p priority after rewrite strips the customer VLAN tag. New [[VPLS]], [[EoMPLS]], [[L2VPN]], and [[PseudowireTransportTypes]] distinguish Type 5, Type 4 passthrough, and Type 4 `transport-mode vlan`, including the important qualification that IOS XR VPLS passthrough does not insert the dummy tag. [[Cisco]] now has a second evidence path as the vendor context for concrete IOS XR encapsulation behavior, and [[CiscoIOSXR]], [[ZhaoCS]], and [[ZhaoCSInfo]] anchor the platform, author, and publication. Eight images were inspected: the topology diagram, VPLS Type 5/Type 4 passthrough captures, rewrite-without-dummy captures, FAT label/control-word captures, the expanded VLAN ID 0 dummy-tag view, and the far-end VLAN 10/PRI 5 verification.

The newest Simon Späti source adds a cautionary dependency layer to the wiki's AI-writing and AI-coding material. New [[AIDependencySkillAtrophy]] says AI assistance becomes harmful when it substitutes for the writing, coding, reading, remembering, and decision practice that forms human skill. [[AIAssistedWriting]] is now more explicitly bounded: AI can help with capture, structure, critique, and optionality, but manual drafting, research struggle, voice, and conviction remain the thinking work. [[AICodingPractice]] now includes a task-horizon warning: autocomplete and small defined functions are different from architecture, planning, and maintainability decisions whose errors compound into the future. [[SimonSpati]] anchors the source as an author who uses AI deliberately but argues that competence, attention, and craft enjoyment are worth preserving. The eight embedded images were inspected and used as evidence for AI productivity/error tradeoffs, reasoning-skill decline, writing overreliance, AI-generated web-content growth, seniority-biased employment effects, and productivity-illusion loops.

The newest Rohan Rajiv source adds a compact persistence frame to the wiki's career and goal-setting material. New [[OneFitSearchMindset]] says that emotionally brutal searches such as graduate-school admissions, job hunting, home buying, or finding a partner should not always be interpreted as requiring broad approval; sometimes the actual success condition is one compatible yes. [[RohanRajiv]] and [[ALearningADay]] anchor the source as a short reflective personal-growth article rather than a general empirical model. The source contains no image references.

The newest Tim Urban source adds a first-principles self-audit layer to [[CareerPlanning]]. New [[WantRealityCareerFramework]] captures the article's model: career options should come from the overlap between authentic wants and realistic reachability, where wants are audited for inherited motives and reality is tested against current career game boards, starting point, success threshold, pace, and persistence. [[TimUrban]] and [[WaitButWhy]] anchor the source's illustrated long-form style. The key framework diagrams were directly inspected and used as evidence for the option pool, Yearning Octopus, yearning hierarchy, strategy loop, opportunity cost, inertia spectrum, and changing-self/changing-world feedback loops; the article also contains many additional illustrative cartoons and repeated footnote icons.

The newest Nicholas Carlini source adds a concrete practitioner taxonomy to the wiki's AI material. New [[PracticalLLMUse]] captures the pattern: current LLMs are useful now for bounded, inspectable work such as application scaffolding, tool tutoring, blank-page code starts, simplification, boilerplate, one-off scripts, API lookup, hard-to-keyword search, teaching, and error fixing. [[NicholasCarlini]] anchors the source as a machine-learning security researcher who is unusually explicit that productivity gains do not erase hallucinations, robustness failures, ethical concerns, privacy and copyright questions, labor issues, misinformation, surveillance, job displacement, or concentration-of-power risks. This strengthens [[AIWorkflowDesign]], [[AICodingPractice]], and [[HumanCodeResponsibility]] by adding a simple task-fit rule: LLM assistance works best when the user can inspect, test, correct, or discard the output.

The newest Morgan Housel source adds a behavioral risk judgment layer to the wiki's investing and decision-making material. New [[BehavioralRiskJudgment]] captures Housel's compact warnings about confirmation, incentives, denial, binary thinking, stale beliefs, overconfidence, regret, and narrow experience. [[InvestmentRiskDiscipline]] now includes need-versus-want risk, debt-versus-savings optionality, future-regret calibration, pessimistic saving, optimistic investing, and the idea that plans should assume plans will fail. [[MorganHousel]] is now represented not only as the author of a timeless business strategy essay but also as an aphoristic behavioral-finance writer connecting money to expectations, time control, reputation, status signaling, and humility. No image references were present in the source Markdown.

The newest MinusX source adds a Claude Code design layer to the wiki's agent material. [[ClaudeCode]] is now framed not only as a powerful command-line coding tool but as a deliberately simple and steerable agent system: one main message history, limited `Task`-style branching, smaller helper-model calls, rich prompt instructions, live code search, a mixed-level tool surface, and model-managed todos. [[AgenticWorkflowPatterns]] gains the one-main-loop plus bounded-branch pattern as a counterweight to opaque multi-agent graphs. [[CodingAgentMinimalTooling]] now distinguishes raw minimalism from deliberately shaped tools: frequent operations such as Edit, Read, Grep/Glob, and TodoWrite can deserve dedicated tools, while shell access remains useful for unusual cases. [[AgenticRAG]] is reinforced by the article's claim that current-code search with ripgrep/read/refine loops can be more debuggable than RAG pipelines whose chunking, similarity, reranking, and freshness choices are hidden. The three embedded images were inspected and used as evidence for Claude Code prompt/update timelines, tool-use frequency, and the simple-versus-branched control loop.

The newest Martin Fowler architecture source adds a scope-sensitive governance layer to the wiki's architecture material. New [[ArchitectureAlignmentForces]] says that coupling, shared code, contribution models, technology choices, and integration patterns should be judged by organizational alignment strength and blast radius rather than by one universal rule. [[MYOB]] now serves as both the technology-radar example and the organization-design case: teams sit inside domains, domains sit inside verticals, and the force of alignment weakens as decisions cross those boundaries. [[DefaultTrialRetire]] and [[TechnologyRadar]] are now connected by scope: informal small-set technology choices fit strong domain forces, while radar-style direction and proposal sharing fit weaker vertical or whole-organization forces. [[IntegrationStrategy]] is qualified by the same model: domain-local APIs, events, or data files can sometimes tolerate tighter coupling, while whole-organization interfaces need schemas, contracts, versioning, backward compatibility, and deprecation discipline. The four embedded diagrams were inspected and used as evidence for team/domain/vertical structure and progressively weaker alignment forces.

The newest Martin Fowler Twitter source adds a social-media curation layer to the wiki's platform, attention, and reading material. New [[SocialMediaCuration]] frames Twitter value as something produced by selective follows, trusted retweets, topical lists, chronological order, reply avoidance, and external workflow handoffs rather than by the default feed alone. [[Twitter]] now includes Fowler's power-user view alongside growth, cultural-metrics, safety, user-tooling, and developer-trust critiques. [[ReadLaterProduct]] and [[Instapaper]] gain a discovery-to-reading pattern: short social posts can point to articles, but saving them for later keeps the feed from becoming the reading environment. [[PlatformAbuseResponse]] is sharpened by Fowler's qualification that personal reply avoidance is easier for users who are not harassment targets; platform-level prevention and serious content-moderation thinking remain necessary. No image references were present in the source Markdown.

The newest Martin Fowler foreword adds an agile-practice layer to the wiki's software-engineering material. New [[AgileSoftwareDevelopment]] frames real agile work as an interconnected system of value focus, teamwork, adaptive planning, customer collaboration, and technical execution rather than a set of ceremonies. New [[ExtremeProgramming]] captures the practice foundation Fowler presents as central to the Agile movement, while [[AgileFluencyModel]] distinguishes basic Scrum-like customer focus from higher fluency that needs technical skill. New [[InternalSoftwareQuality]] names the source's counterintuitive delivery claim: testing, refactoring, design, and collaborative development can decrease cost and increase speed when joined to DevOps culture and [[ContinuousDelivery]]. [[Thoughtworks]], [[MartinFowler]], [[JamesShore]], and [[DianaLarsen]] anchor the practice lineage. No image references were present in the source Markdown.

The newest Andreessen Horowitz source adds a China livestreaming layer to the wiki's mobile, creator, and digital-media material. New [[SocialLivestreaming]] frames the format as front-camera, interaction-centered mobile entertainment: viewers co-produce the show through chat, requests, gifts, and recognition rather than consuming only scheduled talent. New [[DigitalGifting]] captures the monetization loop where virtual goods function as payment, status signal, flirtation, and public message, making [[DigitalMediaMonetization]] less dependent on advertising. New [[LivestreamCommerce]] shows how JD Fresh, [[TaobaoLive]], and [[Xiaomi]] used live video for product demonstration, launches, discounts, and shopping attention, while [[LivestreamingCreatorEconomics]] and [[LivestreamingModeration]] capture the broadcaster incentives, beautification/audio tools, bedroom-studio production tension, talent agencies, and regulatory monitoring needed to sustain the format. The four embedded images were inspected and used as evidence for studio setup, Inke gifting UI, Taobao Live commerce UI, and Inke audio controls.

The newest source adds a motivational layer to the wiki's AI material. [[ActionBiasInAI]] says the first AI-era move is not consuming more success methods but doing concrete work, because real learning comes from confronting actual building problems. [[MaiYang]] and [[NavalRavikant]] anchor this action-first framing, while [[MimeticDesire]] names one failure mode: copying someone else's ambition instead of finding a self-owned desire strong enough to justify tradeoffs.

The newest production database source adds a large-company infrastructure leadership layer to the wiki's reliability and database material. New [[ProductionInfrastructureLeadership]] frames critical infrastructure work as a combined customer, design, review, observability, strategy, and research practice. New [[MaheshBalakrishnan]] and [[Delos]] anchor the case: a Facebook storage system that reached production from a small team, scaled to a much larger organization, and used conservative APIs, staged implementation migration, consistency/durability bias, stricter critical-component review, and implementation-independent observability as operating principles. [[CodeReviewPractice]] is now explicitly risk-sensitive: fast approval remains useful for low-risk work, while critical infrastructure can justify slower review and multiple accepts. [[ServiceObservability]] now includes the Delos-derived rule that measurement should sit above APIs and outside implementations where possible.

The newest Limboy source adds a creative-life layer to the wiki's creator, writing, and AI-workflow material. New [[MakeGoodNewThings]] frames making valuable artifacts as care for others, deep learning, asymmetric upside, and a way to leave remembered knots along one's life rather than only as market output. New [[AIEraCreativeStandards]] captures the article's AI-era quality claim: coding assistants and image tools lower the threshold for creation, but they also make average work cheap, so strong inputs, taste, and standards become more important. New [[CognitiveCuriosity]] distinguishes surface novelty from how-and-why curiosity that gives creative work direction. [[Limboy]] becomes the source-scoped author entity. No image references were present in the source Markdown.

The newest Joel Spolsky source adds a community-mechanics layer to the wiki's product, platform, and behavior-design material. New [[Gamification]] frames points, reputation, and streaks as weak behavioral forces: they can reinforce an activity users already value, but cannot manufacture intrinsic motivation. New [[CommunityReputationSystems]] captures how voting and reputation can rank content, recognize contributors, signal standards, and support moderation, while also making downvotes feel punitive or exclusionary. [[StackOverflow]] now includes both its data-source role and its reputation-based governance role, and [[JoelSpolsky]] becomes the authorial entity for this founder retrospective. The two local images were inspected and treated as decorative photographs rather than source evidence.

The newest Jeff Huang source adds a minimalist work-system layer to the wiki's productivity and personal-knowledge-management material. New [[TextFileProductivity]] captures the workflow where a calendar stores future commitments while a never-ending plain-text file holds each day's bounded plan, notes, completed-work record, and searchable history. [[PersonalProductivity]] gains a concrete alternative to app-heavy task management: size tomorrow's work the night before, split or reschedule oversized tasks, avoid an endlessly postponed todo list, and reduce future workload by deleting or unflagging lower-value commitments. [[PersonalKnowledgeManagement]] gains a chronological work-log pattern where daily lists become meeting minutes, research notes, idea capture, annual-report material, and evidence about what actually happened. [[JeffHuang]] becomes the source-scoped author entity. No image references were present in the source Markdown.

The newest Jason Fried source adds an attention-capacity layer to the wiki's productivity material. [[AttentionManagement]] now distinguishes available time from available attention: a person may be able to squeeze twenty minutes into a day while still lacking the mental presence needed to support another person or project responsibly. [[PersonalProductivity]] gains a sharper qualification to time-management advice: calendar arithmetic is insufficient when the mind is already absorbed by a few key commitments. [[JasonFried]] becomes the source-scoped author entity. No image references were present in the source Markdown.

The newest Jani Mustonen source adds a beginner-programming cognition layer to the wiki's learning and developer-education material. New [[ProgrammerMindset]] names the tacit fluency by which experienced programmers reason about code behavior, line-level details, and whole-program effects. The source qualifies copy-paste learning: examples can teach when learners actively study, modify, and explain them, but not when snippets are treated as magic glue. This connects [[SystematicLearning]], [[ComputationalThinking]], and [[FeynmanTechnique]] to programming pedagogy, and it reinforces [[HumanCodeResponsibility]] by making understanding code behavior part of responsible authorship. No image references were present in the source Markdown.

The newest ecommerce source adds a product-detail-page layer to the wiki's conversion, social-proof, and UX material. New [[ProductPageOptimization]] frames the product page as the place where acquisition effort, product evidence, merchant trust, objection handling, and checkout intent converge. [[ConversionRateOptimization]] gains a fourth surface beyond donation flows, landing pages, and onboarding: product pages may need confidence-building modules such as photos, videos, reviews, FAQs, trust badges, benefit-led copy, mobile purchase paths, speed, and scarcity cues rather than only fewer steps. [[SocialProof]] gains buyer-proximate ecommerce signals including reviews, user-generated content, company logos, and case studies, while [[ProductFlowFriction]] is qualified by the idea that useful page content can reduce uncertainty even when it adds visual weight. The inspected lead illustration supported the product-page system by calling attention to image, copy, CTA, navigation, and supporting modules; the repeated second image reference was actually HTML saved as PNG and could not be used as image evidence.

The newest Legacy Mimic source adds a legacy-modernization transition layer to the wiki's architecture material. New [[LegacyMimic]] captures the temporary compatibility pattern where new components conform to legacy interfaces, events, database schemas, or semantics so incremental [[LegacyDisplacement]] can proceed without breaking unreplaced processes. New [[TransitionalArchitecture]] frames those components as old/new bridgework that should be retired, while [[AntiCorruptionLayer]] is distinguished as potentially enduring model protection for external systems. [[EventInterception]] and [[ExtractValueStreams]] capture the logistics example: sales events are intercepted into a new logistics system, metrics are replicated back into legacy reporting, and a partner-system ACL protects the new logistics model. [[CapabilityOrientedIntegration]] is qualified by the reminder that clean target boundaries may need temporary legacy-shaped interfaces during migration. The inspected diagrams supported these claims by showing the monolith before extraction, logistics split out with mimics and an ACL, and a sequence diagram separating service-providing from service-consuming mimics.

The newest Holden Karnofsky source adds a writing-centered investigation layer to the wiki's learning, reading, and knowledge-output material. New [[LearningByWriting]] frames writing not as a final communication step but as the control surface for learning: state a premature hypothesis, defend it, list weaknesses, read or discuss the subquestion most likely to change the view, revise or switch sides, and repeat. This sharpens [[InformationHierarchy]] by adding support anecdotes where a link's position made it look unsafe to click and absent separate address fields made an available search capability seem removed.

The newest Stratechery source adds a customer-engagement and reporting layer to the wiki's Apple services and growth material. [[AppleRealWorldSocialNetwork]] names [[BenThompson]]'s argument that [[TodayAtApple]] functions as Apple's controlled, retail-based answer to social-network engagement: customers gather around photography, music, coding, creativity, and local talent in a "real social" setting tied to Apple devices and Apple IDs. This sharpens [[AppleMiddleAgeStrategy]], [[AppleGrowthLevers]], and [[AppleServicesMachine]] by adding a measurement critique: if Apple wants investors to value installed-base monetization rather than device units, it should disclose active customers and revenue per user, not only Services revenue and active devices. The inspected chart reinforces the pressure behind that reporting change by showing iPhone unit growth near flat while revenue growth rose through ASP and product mix.

The prior Stratechery source adds a mature-Apple strategy layer to the wiki's Apple services and growth material. [[AppleMiddleAgeStrategy]] names [[BenThompson]]'s argument that [[Apple]]'s high-end smartphone market had saturated enough by 2018 that growth naturally turned inward: higher [[IPhone]] ASPs, more Services revenue, and more Apple-specific devices sold to existing loyal users. This sharpens [[AppleServicesMachine]] and [[AppleGrowthLevers]] by separating Services as financial contribution from Services as hardware differentiation: [[AppleMusic]] may have limited standalone profit, but it can bridge iPhone users toward [[HomePod]] hardware purchases. The source also qualifies [[AppleContentDistributionStrategy]] because Thompson's launch-era HomePod exclusivity argument is later softened by Apple Music's expansion to Alexa.

The newest Complex source adds an early Apple Music culture-platform layer to the wiki's Apple services material. [[AppleMusicCulturePlatform]] names the article's argument that Apple Music was trying to be more than a streaming catalog: [[LarryJackson]] supplied artist collaboration and exclusive-project logic, [[ZaneLowe]] and [[Beats1]] supplied a radio and conversation layer, and [[BozomaSaintJohn]] supplied brand, discovery, and public attention. This sharpens [[AppleMusic]], [[AppleContentDistributionStrategy]], and [[StreamingContentEconomics]] by showing that Apple Music's differentiation depended on human curation, cultural moments, and entertainment-industry relationships as well as subscriber scale and hardware reach. The source is profile-driven and early-stage, and its remote lead image could not be inspected.

The newest Benedict Evans source adds a trust-brand layer to the wiki's Apple services material. [[AppleTrustBrand]] names Evans' argument that Apple's 2019 News+, Arcade, Card, and TV+ event was not only about subscription revenue and iPhone churn reduction, but about making privacy, safety, curation, family-friendly content, and protection from scams into a concrete brand promise. This sharpens [[Apple]] beyond [[AppleServicesMachine]] and [[AppleContentDistributionStrategy]]: services can be economically useful while also reframing Apple as the platform that filters higher-level digital harms such as ad tracking, loot boxes, confusing credit-card charges, phishing, and manipulative ads. The source remains event-scoped because Evans explicitly notes that TV+ price, catalog scale, and spending ambition were still unresolved in April 2019.

The newest Appcanary source adds a programming-language and startup-tooling layer to the wiki's developer experience material. [[PhillipMendoncaVieira]] uses [[Appcanary]]'s discarded [[Clojure]] implementation and return to [[Ruby]] to argue that time-pressed startups should prefer familiar tools and keep attention on the business problem. [[ToolFamiliarity]] names that startup heuristic, while [[DistributedSystemRestraint]] captures the parallel architecture warning: avoid distributed systems until team size, coordination capacity, and product need justify the cost. The source also sharpens [[DeveloperExperience]] and [[DeveloperTooling]] through [[SimpleMadeEasy]]: conceptual simplicity can be real and valuable, but "simple is not easy" becomes harmful when it excuses poor errors, affordances, onboarding, or programmer unhappiness.

The newest VentureBeat/App Annie source adds a quantified app-store economics layer to the wiki's mobile-platform material. [[MobileAppStoreEconomics]] captures the split: in 2015 [[GooglePlay]] generated twice as many downloads as Apple's [[AppStore]], while Apple's store generated 75% more revenue. This sharpens [[MobileEcosystem]], [[Android]], and [[IOS]] by separating platform reach from monetization: emerging markets such as Brazil, India, Indonesia, Turkey, and Mexico drove Google Play download growth, while China, the U.S., and Japan drove iOS App Store revenue growth. [[Apple]] therefore gains a concrete 2015 example of smaller-but-higher-spending ecosystem economics, while [[Google]] and [[GooglePlay]] gain a counterbalancing volume-strength profile.

The newest SQLite production source adds a single-machine database simplicity layer to the wiki's architecture material. [[SQLiteProductionTradeoffs]] frames SQLite as a legitimate production choice when an app can run on one durable machine, stays mostly read-heavy, keeps writes short, and values lower operational overhead more than distributed database machinery. [[SQLite]] sharpens [[DatabaseConsolidation]] and [[TechnologyStackComplexity]] by showing that simplification can remove the database service entirely, not just consolidate workloads into PostgreSQL. The qualification is the heart of the source: multi-machine high availability, network or ephemeral file systems, heavy parallel writes, long transactions, live backups, and migration tooling can make PostgreSQL or MySQL the simpler production choice. [[DatabaseTransactionIsolation]] captures the transaction-specific lesson, including the inspected isolation table where serializable isolation prevents dirty, non-repeatable, and phantom reads while weaker levels admit more anomalies.

The newest Mission.org source adds an opportunity-cost layer to the wiki's goal, attention, discipline, and productivity material. [[OpportunityCost]] names the article's "pay the price" frame: ambitious personal change is not just wanting an outcome but accepting the cost of fewer directions, fewer merely good options, and fewer low-value defaults. This sharpens [[GoalSetting]] by making decision and exclusion central, [[SelfDiscipline]] by treating daily refusals as the actual payment, [[AttentionManagement]] by making spare minutes and phone use with loved ones evidence of priority, and [[PersonalProductivity]] by framing time as the scarce resource that cannot be recovered. The synthesis is qualified because the article's "anything is possible" rhetoric is motivational rather than proof that personal discipline can overcome every structural, health, caregiving, or material constraint.

The newest Fast Company privacy source adds a class-differentiated privacy layer to the wiki's governance, work, and digital-rights material. [[PrivacyPovertyDivide]] names the source's core claim: poor and marginalized people often surrender more data and accept more monitoring to access welfare, employment, housing, credit, prison communication, or basic services, while affluent people receive many government transfers with fewer intrusive checks. [[WelfareSurveillance]] traces that burden from colonial overseers of the poor through home visits, drug tests, fingerprinting, biometrics, and cross-database verification. [[DataBrokerPersistence]] and [[AlgorithmicDecisionOpacity]] show how old, inaccurate, or hidden records can deny benefits, housing, jobs, and loans in ways lawyers struggle to contest. The source also complicates privacy absolutism through [[SurveillanceGap]]: undocumented immigrants, day laborers, homeless people, and people with convictions can be harmed by too little usable documentation as well as too much surveillance, making meaningful control over disclosure the stronger goal.

The newest Andre Staltz source adds an open-Web decline layer to the wiki's platform-power material. [[WebCentralization]] distinguishes internet growth from Web health: Staltz argues that Google, Facebook, and Amazon can keep internet usage rising while making independent, browser-mediated publishing less necessary. [[BrowserBypass]] names the mechanism across the three companies: Google moves from search toward AI suggestion, assistants, AMP, and proprietary cloud infrastructure; Facebook consolidates social traffic through apps, messaging, Instant Articles, and AR/VR ambitions; and Amazon routes commerce through retail scale, apps, Echo, and cloud services. [[Trinet]] is the source's speculative endpoint, a warning model in which network access and infrastructure optimize for the three dominant platform networks while open-Web freedom, anonymity, startup independence, and account-level recourse weaken.

The newest Andrew Chen career source adds a future-option layer to the wiki's career-planning material. [[NextNextJobFramework]] asks people to name the job after the next job, diagnose why it is not reachable now, and choose current opportunities by how well they close gaps in skills, network, experiences, mentors, ideas, or a decisive superpower. This sharpens [[CareerPlanning]] beyond fit, promotion ladders, side projects, and freelancing experiments: a current role can be a stepping stone when it makes the later role more attainable, as Chen says [[Uber]] did for his eventual startup-investing path. The framework is still qualified by emotion and uncertainty; culture, manager fit, compensation, and excitement matter, and sometimes the real barrier to a desired future role is risk aversion rather than missing credentials.

The newest Andrew Chen founder-pitch source adds a social-modesty layer to the wiki's startup communication material. [[DinnerPartyJerkTest]] names Chen's diagnostic for whether a founder pitch is too restrained: if describing the team's credentials, earned secrets, early proof points, traction, ambition, and upside would not feel awkward at a friendly dinner party, it may not be explicit enough for investors, employees, partners, or journalists. [[StartupVisionSelling]] therefore becomes less only about concise vision and more about a mode switch: founders must communicate the future strongly enough for stakeholders to perceive adventure, ambition, and exceptional fit, while still keeping clear operational judgment about missing [[ProductMarketFit]], unit-economics gaps, marketing gaps, and team risks.

The newest Andrew Chen writing-output source adds a cadence and feedback layer to the wiki's AI-assisted and explanatory-writing material. [[AndrewChen]] argues that writing more depends on a system: collect raw ideas continuously, give yourself permission to publish small posts, reuse templates such as reviews, quotes, lessons learned, Q&A, topical links, and reflections, protect scheduled writing time, and remove distractions with dedicated devices or phone boundaries. [[AIAssistedWriting]] is present, but as a support layer for brainstorming, topic sentences, and voice cleanup rather than the whole practice. [[CreatorFeedbackLoop]] sharpens because Chen recommends testing short posts first, expanding what resonates into threads, and turning the strongest ideas into essays; this directly qualifies perfectionist [[ExplanatoryWriting]] by treating an early obsession with quality as a way to procrastinate and block style experiments.

The newest [[Tw93]] source adds an engineer-facing investing and leverage layer to the wiki's finance and creator-work material. [[EngineerInvestment]] frames investing as domain judgment under risk: engineers may understand AI, semiconductors, software, cloud, and Bitcoin-adjacent themes, but the source insists that technical conviction must be checked against business quality, future cash flows, financial statements, valuation, and downside math. [[InvestmentRiskDiscipline]] captures the strongest negative rules: avoid margin, shorting, unfamiliar assets, frequent trading, short-term speculation, and blind high-point chasing. [[IndexFundStrategy]] becomes the simpler alternative through low-cost S&P 500 and Nasdaq ETF exposure, while [[EngineerLeverage]] broadens investment beyond markets by treating code, writing, independent products, and sharing as ways to turn expertise into reusable assets.

The newest Andrew Chen AI-blogging source adds a pragmatic writer-workflow layer to the wiki's AI-assisted writing material. [[AIAssistedWriting]] now includes Chen's distinction between weak default prose and useful creative scaffolding: ChatGPT drafts can be stiff, generic, and under-evidenced, but they still reduce blank-page friction by giving the author something to criticize, replace, and rewrite. [[AIWorkflowDesign]] broadens from controlled pipelines into exploratory loops of rough drafting, question generation, outlines, voice cleanup, tone passes, and WordPress-side iteration. [[ChatGPT]] is therefore represented not only as a fact-checking support tool but also as a blogging companion whose value depends on human selection, examples, story, statistics, voice, and final judgment.

The newest Andrew Chen click-friction source adds an onboarding and conversion layer to the wiki's product-growth material. [[ProductFlowFriction]] names Chen's heuristic that every extra click, field, install, tutorial, or signup demand spends scarce user intent, so critical flows should remove steps that delay the core product experience. The source also qualifies low-friction growth: some friction is justified when it improves later product value, reactivation, collaboration, or app richness, and more raw signups do not necessarily become proportionally more paying customers. This sharpens [[ConversionRateOptimization]] by tying step reduction to downstream user quality rather than treating signup volume as the only goal.

The newest Andrew Chen source adds a creator-economy startup layer to the wiki's startup, marketplace, and creator-work material. [[CreatorEconomyStartups]] are framed as promising but structurally difficult because they inherit a [[CreatorPowerLaw]], compete for scarce profile distribution through [[LinkInBioCompetition]], face the [[CreatorGraduationProblem]] when top creators can leave or renegotiate take rates, and suffer [[AlgorithmicFeastAndFamine]] from social-feed dependence. Chen's bullish version of the sector looks less like a thin tip jar and more like AI- or video-first, managed marketplace-like infrastructure that brings demand, proprietary functionality, durable subscriptions, and higher-value niche monetization to creators rather than merely renting their existing audience.

The newest Karpathy source adds a technical-accessibility layer to the wiki's learning and explanation material. [[AndrejKarpathy]] uses [[Micrograd]] as a compact case: the code was already short, commented, documented, and conceptually minimal, yet broader engagement arrived only after he built a from-scratch video walkthrough. [[TechnicalAccessibility]] names the durable claim: technical artifacts need ramps that lower the initial cost of engagement, because even expert audiences may skip work they could understand if the entry path feels too effortful. This strengthens [[ExplanatoryWriting]] and [[FromScratchProtocolLearning]] by separating artifact quality from approachability.

The newest Stefanie Williams source adds a counterargument to the Talia Jane/Yelp worker-precarity thread. [[StefanieWilliams]] rejects Jane's wage-and-cost framing and uses her own post-2008 service-work path to argue that early-career hardship should be met through roommates, commuting, second jobs, lower-status service work, and humility. [[WorkEthicPersonalResponsibility]] names that frame: available paid work and practical tradeoffs are treated as more responsible than public appeals for help or blaming employers. This directly qualifies [[EmployeeFinancialPrecarity]] and [[TaliaJane]] by showing that the same Yelp/Eat24 dispute can be interpreted either as structural cash-flow insecurity in a tech-adjacent job or as avoidable individual choices.

The newest Talia Jane source adds a lower-paid labor and cost-of-living layer to the wiki's workplace and startup material. [[TaliaJane]] describes working in [[Eat24]] customer support under [[Yelp]] while rent, transit, utilities, medical copays, debt, and food costs left basic needs precarious. [[EmployeeFinancialPrecarity]] names the source's central claim: employment inside a well-funded technology company does not guarantee security when compensation fails to match local living costs. The source also qualifies [[StartupCulture]] and [[WorkEnvironment]] by showing how office snacks, executive wealth, public values, and always-on product promises can coexist with workers who cannot afford groceries or reliable transportation to work.

The newest Startup Security source adds an early-stage cloud security layer to the wiki's infrastructure and startup material. [[Magoo]] frames [[StartupSecurityDebt]] as predictable design debt that founding teams can avoid while still supporting reliability and developer velocity. [[CentralizedLogging]] becomes the first operational primitive because queryable application, system, CloudTrail, and network-flow logs support both incident response and availability troubleshooting. [[CloudAccountSegmentation]], [[ProductionAccessControl]], [[NetworkSegmentation]], and [[SecretManagement]] extend that model: account boundaries control blast radius, bastions and temporary access make production administration rare, public/private network placement protects internal services, and early secrets handling avoids leaked keys and later application rewrites. The source also sharpens [[InfrastructureAsCode]] by treating Terraform, CloudFormation, review, tests, and CI/CD execution as safeguards against infrastructure drift.

The newest Appster source adds an app-specific landing-page layer to the wiki's startup marketing and conversion material. [[AppLandingPages]] names the article's model: a standalone page with one conversion goal can validate app demand before code exists, drive downloads outside app-store constraints, collect lead demographics, and measure campaign messaging. The inspected screenshots turn the checklist into concrete evidence: WhatsApp shows a focused app page, [[Slack]] pairs value proposition with product UI and testimonial support, Evernote foregrounds one sign-up CTA, Paleo Leap illustrates CTA overload, Breather and Huemor show different coherent visual strategies, and Zendesk shows how vague headline hierarchy can hide the clearer product explanation. This strengthens [[ConversionRateOptimization]], [[SocialProof]], and [[InformationHierarchy]] with a pre-product marketing surface where clarity, proof, speed, and ongoing testing matter together.

The newest LatePost interview adds a hardware-founder and organizational-maturity case to the wiki's entrepreneurship material. [[WangTao]] is presented as moving from product passion, competitive ego, and an old "world is stupid" posture toward self-critique, truth-seeking, and management learning. [[DJI]] becomes a case where integrated hardware innovation produced a global drone and imaging company, but rapid growth also exposed corruption, factional power centers, and the weakness of a product-only culture. [[EntropyReductionManagement]] names Wang's later model: clear goals, transparent processes, measurable results, contribution-linked incentives, stronger managers, and systems that counter organizational drift. This extends [[FounderLedOrganizationalEvolution]] beyond market-facing business-model pivots into the harder problem of turning founder taste and talent density into durable organizational capacity.

The newest Coin and Crypto source adds a speculative cryptocurrency-payments scenario to the wiki's platform and payments material. [[Bitcoin]] is framed as the incumbent cryptocurrency whose currency ambitions depend on moving beyond investment hype into merchant acceptance, but whose volatility, hack-recovery risk, and transaction throughput could weaken it at large retail scale. [[Amazon]] becomes the market-shaping platform in this scenario: the article argues that Amazon could hurt Bitcoin by staying out of crypto payments, choosing a faster rival such as [[Ethereum]] or Ripple, or creating its own token for Prime, Twitch, Audible, and purchase discounts. [[CryptocurrencyMerchantAdoption]] captures the durable synthesis while keeping the source scoped: large merchants can validate or redirect payment ecosystems, but the article does not prove Amazon's actual later crypto strategy.

The newest Darius Foroux source adds a pragmatic self-education investment frame to the wiki's learning cluster. [[SelfEducationInvestment]] names the article's claim that education is a recurring input rather than a one-time credential: knowledge is perishable, so people need repeated reading, research, practice, and exposure to new ideas. [[DariusForoux]] connects this to practical resilience rather than school identity: learning improves decisions, expands opportunity, can make workers or entrepreneurs less interchangeable, and remains useful after money, clients, reputation, or jobs disappear. The inspected image reinforces the thesis visually by pointing "Always invest in this thing" at a brain, while the concept remains qualified by existing [[FreeLearning]] and [[CoerciveLearning]] pages because sustainable education should protect curiosity rather than become imposed pressure.

The newest codebase tutorial adds a compact implementation example to the wiki's coding-agent retrieval thread. [[Cursor]] is the reference product: its codebase feature is described as vectorizing functions, classes, and logic blocks so similar code can support repository-grounded question answering. The tutorial's [[Agno]] implementation deliberately avoids a vector store, instead exposing `search_codebase` and `read_file_segment` tools to an agent with separate instructions for log troubleshooting and code-structure analysis. This strengthens [[AgenticRAG]] and [[CodingAgentMinimalTooling]] with inspected runtime evidence: screenshots show the agent searching memory-related terms, reading `pkg/memory.go` and `pkg/cpu.go`, and producing a cgroup-based explanation of memory accounting from the current repository.

The newest Brad Ellis source adds a physical ergonomics layer to the wiki's mobile and UX material. [[IOS]] is no longer only a platform-control surface; it is also a design environment where larger screens can make inherited top-navbar conventions harder to use. [[ThumbReachErgonomics]] names the constraint shown in the inspected touch-zone images: large phones move top corners out of natural one-handed reach, leaving frequent actions better suited to the lower part of the screen. [[ReachNavigation]] names Ellis's proposed response: use sheets, exposed drawers, bottom controls, in-content destination buttons, and broad swipe gestures for common navigation, while reserving harder-to-reach placement for dangerous actions where accidental taps would be costly.

The newest Mark Suster source adds a capital-intensive local-operations startup case to the wiki's product, marketplace, and scaling material. [[Bird]] is framed as a category-creating [[Micromobility]] company whose early Santa Monica usage gave [[MarkSuster]] confidence before the $300 million funding headline; inspected images show Suster and another Upfront attendee on Bird scooters and a dense beach-path cluster of parked Birds. [[ElectricScooterServiceDefensibility]] names the source's bundled moat argument: capital, [[DocklessFleetDensity]], vehicle design, route and placement data, local charger and mechanic networks, battery yield, and [[BrandDistinctiveness]] can make a seemingly copyable scooter service harder to replicate. The article qualifies that optimism with safety, helmet adoption, seasonality, supply constraints, and likely competition from [[Uber]].

The newest Tom Tunguz source adds an innovation-through-combination layer to the wiki's learning, data, and SaaS material. [[InnovationAtIntersection]] names the source's main pattern: new ideas often come from recombining older ideas across fields, as [[MickPearce]]'s termite-inspired [[EastgateCentre]] example illustrates. [[BenjaminJones]] adds the modern specialization pressure: the decline of the Renaissance-person model means innovation increasingly depends on teams with complementary expertise. [[OrganizationalDataSharing]] translates that claim into SaaS operations, where customer success, sales, marketing, finance, [[TwilioSegment]] Sources, and [[Looker]] Blocks can connect fragmented observations into end-to-end funnel hypotheses.

The newest Alexandra Noonan source adds a software-architecture case where the correct boundary changed over time. [[TwilioSegment]] initially used microservices to solve [[HeadOfLineBlocking]] in its server-side destinations pipeline: inspected diagrams show retry traffic in one shared queue delaying all destinations, then a router distributing work to separate destination queues. As integrations grew, [[MicroserviceOperationalOverhead]] became the larger problem because each destination added repos, queues, services, dependency versions, load profiles, autoscaling tuning, and on-call burden. [[MonolithConsolidation]] names the reversal: [[Centrifuge]] replaced per-destination queues, destination code moved into one monorepo with [[MonorepoDependencyConvergence]], and [[TrafficRecorder]] enabled [[RecordedTrafficTesting]] so 140-plus destination tests no longer depended on live partner APIs. The source qualifies monolith enthusiasm by keeping fault isolation, cache efficiency, and dependency-update blast radius visible as costs.

The newest Luca Dellanna source adds a trust-transfer layer to the wiki's marketplace and platform material. [[AggregationTheory]] is framed as more than demand control and matching: in markets where customers cannot quickly assess unfamiliar suppliers, popularity acts as a trust proxy, so known suppliers capture disproportionate profits. [[MarketplaceTrust]] now includes the strategic effect of aggregators such as [[Airbnb]] and [[Uber]] becoming trusted by demand; reviews, payment systems, insurance, reimbursement, dispatch, and delisting make stranger transactions acceptable, flattening supplier profit while centralizing trust and profit at the platform layer. [[TrustMinimizationTechnology]] names Dellanna's proposed pressure point: smart contracts, smart locks, self-driving cars, or similar low-human-action systems may erode the portion of aggregator value tied to trust enablement, even if incumbent demand ownership remains hard to attack.

The newest Andrew Chen source adds a pre-product-market-fit survival layer to the startup cluster. [[TroughOfSorrow]] names the period after launch attention and novelty fade but before [[ProductMarketFit]] is clear; the inspected [[YCombinator]] diagram shows that path as a TechCrunch spike, novelty decay, the trough, improvement releases, false hope, possible crashes, and eventual recovery. [[AndrewChen]] argues that founders need both emotional steadiness and diagnosis: cofounder conflict, churn, and discouragement are common, but the analytical response is to identify whether the real bottleneck is product quality, onboarding, marketing, or growth execution. This sharpens [[StartupRunway]] and [[StartupFocus]] because capital buys product iterations only if the team uses those iterations on the right root problem rather than reflexively rebooting or adding generic growth tactics.

The newest Andrew Chen fitness note adds a longevity-oriented capacity-reserve thread. [[AndrewChen]] shares a [[VO2Max]] graph from [[PeterAttia]]'s [[Outlive]] that compares high, average, and low [[CardiorespiratoryFitness]] percentiles across age against activity thresholds such as walking, jogging, carrying weight upstairs, and briskly climbing stairs. The inspected chart shows all curves declining with age, but high fitness preserves far more later-life margin; Chen's practical inference is that building cardiovascular capacity earlier is more plausible than expecting a late jump from average or low fitness to the 95th percentile. This source is personal and chart-driven rather than clinical, so the new synthesis is a behavior-change heuristic, not a full exercise prescription.

The newest Google Design source adds a redesign-case-building layer to the wiki's product and UX material. [[ProductRedesign]] is framed as a team alignment problem before it is a screen-design exercise: the [[Crashlytics]] team used the move from [[Fabric]] into [[Firebase]] and [[MaterialDesign]] as a chance to repair deeper design debt. [[UserJourneyMapping]] surfaced four critical journeys and the recurring [[InvestigateAndFixFlow]], while [[InternalCoDesign]] paper-cutout sessions turned long-tenured team knowledge into independent pain-point evidence. The resulting diagnosis was [[InformationHierarchy]]: users scrolled, clicked through less important UI, and sometimes requested features that already existed because key crash data and capabilities were buried. Inspected screenshots reinforce the claim by showing the Firebase redesign pulling crash-free statistics, event trends, filters, issue tables, device/version details, session tabs, logs, keys, data, and stack traces into clearer overview and issue-detail surfaces.

The newest Mobile Dev Memo source adds a monetization layer to the wiki's mobile messaging thread. [[EricSeufert]] argues that [[MobileMessagingAdvertising]] in early 2016 clustered around opt-in brand channels, CRM-like brand conversations, sponsored content, and branded stickers rather than simple banner transplantation. [[FacebookMessenger]] is the main case: an alleged leaked plan suggested ads in brand threads users had previously initiated, while a sticker-store screenshot shows a free Despicable Me 2 branded pack as ad-adjacent inventory. [[Kik]], [[Snapchat]], [[WeChat]], [[Tango]], [[BlackBerryMessenger]], and [[LINE]] broaden the taxonomy, and [[WhatsApp]] qualifies it by showing that even Facebook-owned messaging products had public anti-ad positioning.

The newest Stratechery source adds a productivity-software business-model layer to the wiki's SaaS and platform material. [[BenThompson]] argues that [[Adobe]]'s move from packaged software to [[CreativeCloud]] subscriptions matters because [[Photoshop]]-style tools create extreme value variance: casual users resist large upfront prices, professionals receive career-scale value, and students may become valuable only after learning the tool. [[ProductivityAppSubscriptions]] and [[SubscriptionSurplusAlignment]] name the source's broader claim that recurring pricing can lower entry friction, fund maintenance, and let producer revenue rise as user value grows. The platform twist is [[PlatformStickiness]]: if serious productivity apps become viable and platform-specific, [[Apple]], [[Google]], [[Microsoft]], [[IOS]], and [[Android]] have reason to support subscriptions because users who depend on indispensable apps are less likely to switch ecosystems.

The newest AVC source adds an investing-capacity frame to the wiki's startup-finance material. [[FredWilson]] defines [[ActiveInvesting]] as capital plus time, energy, intellect, control, or leadership, whether that means board-seat activism, real-estate development, hard-money lending, or leading a seed round. [[PassiveInvesting]] is not dismissed, but Wilson argues it fits best with liquid markets and diversification because exit substitutes for direct control. [[PortfolioConcentration]] captures the source's sharper warning for angel, seed, and VC markets: if every active investment requires real attention, investors cannot scale indefinitely while honestly claiming to be active in every position.

The newest Product Habits source adds a retention-first SaaS growth layer. [[HitenShah]] argues that SaaS acquisition became easier as knowledge, tools, freemium entry, and distribution got cheaper, but those same forces made [[SaaSRetention]] harder by increasing competition, lowering switching costs, and bringing in weak-fit leads. [[ProductLedRetention]] names the source's answer: product strength, suite expansion, account expansion, onboarding into deeper use, and marketing aligned to sticky customer value matter more than raw acquisition volume. [[Intercom]] illustrates broader workflow coverage, [[Front]] illustrates retention-led upsell and net negative churn, and [[CrazyEgg]] illustrates differentiating against [[GoogleAnalytics]] through heatmap-focused product-message fit. This also qualifies [[CustomerAcquisitionCost]] and [[CustomerLifetimeValue]]: CAC can rise in saturated markets, and LTV depends on customers continuing to choose the product after switching barriers fall.

The newest accounting primer adds a finance-domain modeling layer to the wiki's software-design material. [[JohnMcKee]] and [[TomMornini]] present [[DoubleEntryAccounting]] as a compact business language that developers should understand when writing code to track money. [[AccountingSoftwareArchitecture]] captures the source's warning that many products make accounting look mysterious because they act like business-document databases that produce accounting reports rather than pure accounting systems. [[FinancialSoftwareDesign]] and [[BusinessFinanceLiteracy]] therefore become engineering concerns: the source's point is not merely that accountants use different words, but that incorrect domain models can be baked into software when developers do not understand accounting's underlying structure. The source is incomplete and ends mid-history, so its historical claims around [[LucaPacioli]] and pre-1494 accounting origins remain qualified.

The ipSpace.net source adds a networking-specific automation design layer. [[IvanPepelnjak]] argues that [[NetworkAutomation]] is theoretically possible for any precisely described operation, but practically constrained by the cost of describing and maintaining operations in snowflake network designs. Automation therefore joins security, convergence, latency, jitter, and reliability as one requirement in the architecture tradeoff set rather than a reason to flatten every network by default. This also sharpens [[InfrastructureAsCode]] and [[ChangeSafety]]: automation code is executable operational knowledge, so it must stay synchronized with real network design or it can become a direct source of failure.

The newest Register source adds a concrete tool-and-vendor layer to [[NetworkAutomation]]. [[Ansible]]'s network expansion brought command, configuration, and template modules into Ansible 2.0 Playbooks, with initial support for [[AristaNetworks]], [[Cisco]], [[Juniper]], [[CumulusNetworks]], and [[OpenSwitch]] while [[Huawei]] remained absent. [[PeterSprygada]]'s framing connects the launch to configuration automation, existing-state validation, and continuous compliance against drift, qualifying automation as both a multivendor tooling problem and a [[ChangeSafety]] practice rather than just faster cut-and-paste configuration.

The newest Networklore benchmark adds a tool-fit and performance layer to [[NetworkAutomation]]. [[PatrickOgenstad]] compares [[Ansible]] and [[Nornir]] on local template generation before any network I/O, showing [[Nornir]] rising from 0.621 seconds at 100 hosts to 17.217 seconds at 10,000 hosts while Ansible rises from 18.217 seconds to 41 minutes 22.106 seconds. The inspected charts make the contrast visible: Nornir nearly disappears beside Ansible on the shared axis, while the Nornir-only view shows roughly linear growth. This qualifies Ansible's existing role in the wiki by separating network-automation capability from suitability for every data-heavy or schedule-bound workflow.

The Airbnb data-science source adds a career-transition and company-practice layer to the wiki's data material. [[AcademicIndustryDataScienceTransition]] captures the article's central move: academic research skill can transfer into industry, but only when paired with beginner's mindset, business-domain framing, audience-sensitive communication, and willingness to ship useful first versions. [[IndustryDataScience]] names the operating model behind that transition: data scientists at [[Airbnb]] use statistics, practical data munging, experimentation, and machine learning to improve company metrics and user experience, while also checking whether labels, logs, instrumentation, and model metrics actually connect to the business problem. This qualifies [[DataScienceTechnologyAdoption]] by showing that adoption is not just Python, R, or package traffic; it also includes organizational roles, knowledge repositories, seminars, mentorship, and other structures that make data work reusable.

The newest Data Dependence tutorial adds a beginner scientific-computing layer to that data-science adoption thread. [[Jamal]] presents [[NumPy]] as the practical foundation for [[ScientificPython]] because it gives [[Python]] C-backed arrays for vector and matrix work that plain Python cannot match. [[NumPyArrayModel]] captures the source's basic representation: one-dimensional arrays can stand for vectors, nested sequences make matrices and higher-dimensional arrays, and properties such as shape, `itemsize`, `ndim`, and `nbytes` help users inspect them. [[MultidimensionalArraySlicing]], [[VectorizedArrayOperations]], and [[BooleanMasking]] name the tutorial's working techniques, with the inspected images showing colored 2D slice expressions, a dot-product scalar calculation, and conditional point selection on a sine curve.

The newest Above Avalon source adds a corporate-giant fragility frame around the Apple cluster. [[NeilCybart]] argues that the 2018 race to a trillion-dollar market cap among [[Apple]], [[Amazon]], [[Google]], and [[Microsoft]] mattered less than the broader question of whether Apple, Amazon, Alphabet/Google, Microsoft, and [[Facebook]] had become permanently entrenched giants. The inspected chart qualifies bubble fears by showing top-five S&P 500 concentration was higher in much of the 1960s and 1970s than the 16.5% level cited for 2018, but Cybart also rejects permanence: cash, data, software prowess, R&D, and huge user bases give flexibility without abolishing [[CorporateGiantFragility]]. For Apple specifically, the source reframes [[AppleProductTheory]] and [[AppleGrowthLevers]] around process: Apple's future depends less on the iPhone, Watch, or Services individually than on its ability to keep creating valuable tools through collaboration, design, core-technology ownership, market timing, and willingness to change.

The newest Above Avalon source adds pricing strategy to the Apple cluster. [[NeilCybart]] argues that [[Apple]] used [[AirPods]] at $159 and [[AppleWatch]] Series 1 at $269 to push wearables toward mass-market adoption while still moving deeper into luxury-brand territory. [[ApplePricingStrategy]] names the pattern: lower entry prices grow the user base, premium SKUs such as Apple Watch Hermès and Edition serve higher-end segments, and Apple's balance sheet, supply chain, larger component orders, owned silicon, and vertical integration make aggressive pricing harder for smaller competitors to match. This qualifies [[WearableComputing]] and [[AppleGrowthLevers]] by showing that adoption was not only a form-factor or installed-base story; price, segmentation, and accessible luxury were part of the mechanism.

The newest Above Avalon source sharpens the Apple Services thread. [[NeilCybart]] argues that [[Apple]] Services was not proof of a services-company pivot, but a hardware-dependent [[AppleServicesMachine]] built from digital content, iCloud, AppleCare, Apple Pay, and licensing. The embedded Services diagram is direct evidence for that category structure, while Cybart's 2017 estimates make the revenue mix concrete: about $31B in reported Services revenue, roughly $21B from digital content, about $11B retained from App Store commissions, and about $4B from licensing. This qualifies [[AppleGrowthLevers]] and [[AppleContentDistributionStrategy]] by showing that Services growth rested on Apple's installed base and content distribution economics rather than standing apart from hardware.

The newest Above Avalon source makes the Apple product-strategy cluster more explicit. [[AppleProductTheory]] names [[NeilCybart]]'s ladder from Mac desktops to Mac portables, iPad, [[IPhone]], [[AppleWatch]], and possible [[SmartGlasses]]: each category handles tasks formerly assigned to a larger or less personal computer. The embedded diagram is direct evidence for that model, placing glasses below Watch as a device meant to take tasks from both Watch and iPhone. The 2018 iPhone XS/XR and Apple Watch Series 4 launches are interpreted as current clues: A12 Bionic silicon and smarter cameras make iPhone a stronger AR navigator and computer alternative, while Watch heart and fall features show proactive body-centered computing that phones cannot naturally absorb.

Another Above Avalon source adds an operating-growth layer to the Apple cluster. [[NeilCybart]] argues that [[Apple]]'s 2018 revenue rebound depended on three uneven [[AppleGrowthLevers]]: higher [[IPhone]] average selling prices, Services growth, and [[WearableComputing]] adoption through [[AppleWatch]] and [[AirPods]]. The embedded chart supports the rebound by showing TTM revenue rising from roughly $215B in 4Q16 to about $255B in 3Q18, up 17% over seven quarters. The source qualifies the existing smart-glasses and content-distribution thread by showing a transition: iPhone ASP drove most near-term growth, but Services and wearables looked more durable as future engines because they could compound across Apple's installed base.
